name: Samoa
summary: A red field with a blue canton bearing five white stars of the Southern Cross. Adopted in 1948–1949 under New Zealand administration and kept at independence in 1962.
origin: Under New Zealand trusteeship, Samoa adopted a red flag with a blue canton and four stars in 1948. A fifth, smaller star was added on 24 February 1949. The flag was kept when Samoa became independent on 1 January 1962, the first Pacific island nation to do so.

symbols.name: Southern Cross
symbols.description: Four large and one small white stars in the canton.
symbols.meaning: Samoa's place in the southern hemisphere.

facts: Samoa was the first Pacific island nation to gain independence, in 1962.
In 2011 Samoa moved west of the International Date Line, skipping 30 December.
Taiwan's flag has a similar layout with a white sun in the canton.
clues: Red with a blue canton holding five white stars of the Southern Cross.
The flag of the first Pacific island nation to become independent.
Its country skipped a whole day in 2011 by moving across the date line.
